bullets: Risk lives in the couplings, not the components — the dangerous risks are the slow correlations between parts rather than individual component failures.
The framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you're making — the version of the question that actually matters is what tradeoffs are being chosen.
Some components have reliability issues, and teams using a paid set say display out — reliability crosscuts everything and is where the last stretch of risk management focus should go.
If you ignore the tat, you end up rebuilding it from scratch a year later — ignoring the underlying coupling or framing leads to costly rework.
Systems thinking and risk management intersect through vocabularies and taxonomies — the disciplines share a common language for describing interactions and tradeoffs.
The dangerous risks are discount — the most underrated piece of risk management is discounting slow, correlated risks rather than obvious component failures.
A practical takeaway: pick one of the ideas covered and run it for two weeks — testing a single concept in practice reveals its real tradeoffs.
